A1.justification: Despite the new title and renaming HVL to HVLFormer, both PDFs describe the same research lineage and four segmentation benchmarks. All pages, tables, figures and equations were readable. V2 ends with references; v3 includes a seven-page supplement.

before.justification: V2 reports original segmentation results on four datasets, class-wise IoUs, component and loss ablations, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results, expanded component and sensitivity experiments, qualitative predictions, and an appendix pixel-text alignment evaluation.

M1.justification: V3 adds GPT-4o-generated dataset-conditioned descriptions and replaces CLIP zero-shot class relevance with a trained adapter. PTRM changes from bidirectional cross-attention to convolutional spatial gating. The additional instance-level query set in v2's DQTD disappears, and mask/class aggregation changes. V2's topology/anchor and class-occlusion regularizers are replaced by TQDM-derived regularization and layer-wise cross-view/modal consistency. These are substantive procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate semi-supervised semantic segmentation on Pascal VOC, COCO, ADE20K and Cityscapes. The additional prompting analyses and qualitative examples reuse this coverage; no new evaluated dataset, domain or task is established.

E2.justification: V3 adds reported comparisons with TQDM and Pseudo-SD across all four benchmarks, and POS on VOC, COCO and Cityscapes. It removes DualTeacher from VOC and several Cityscapes comparators, including CPS and U2PL. The component-ablation baseline changes from Mask2Former to TQDM. Figure 1 also reattributes identical prediction panels from SemiVL to UniMatch V2 without explaining the change.

E3.justification: The main benchmark splits, crop sizes and epoch budgets remain unchanged. Implementation statements change from one textual query per class to three, while COCO comparator backbones change from Xception-60 to XC65. New analyses introduce controlled hierarchy/threshold settings and a mean-cosine-similarity evaluation in A.5. These reported settings do not establish that every retained benchmark experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2's VOC component and regularization ablations are replaced by cumulative HTQG/PTRM/CMCR studies on low- and higher-label VOC and COCO splits. V3 adds prompting comparisons, absent-class weighting variants, hierarchy-depth sensitivity, PTRM versus cross-attention comparisons, and quantitative alignment analysis. The class-wise without-HTQG row disappears, while Figures A.1-A.5 add qualitative cases across the four datasets.

E5.justification: V2 gives no run or seed count. V3 Section 4.1 newly states that results are averaged over three random data-sampling seeds. Neither version reports dispersion, confidence intervals or significance tests. This establishes additional reporting, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: The EVA02-L benchmark mIoUs are retained, but some ViT-B results change: VOC-92 goes from 87.1 to 85.4 and Cityscapes-186 from 79.0 to 79.9. Class-wise results change, and extensive comparator, ablation and alignment results are added, including 0.54/0.62/0.77 in Table A.2. These concern revised methods, not controlled same-procedure improvements. V3's ADE20K-158 gain reporting is inconsistent: 41.6 versus TQDM's 25.3 implies 16.3, not the stated baseline gain of 13.5.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation changes substantially: spatial-gating equations replace PTRM's softmax-attention update, and new CMCR and inherited regularization objectives replace v2's topology/anchor and masked-feature objectives. Appendix A.2 additionally defines cross-scale refinement for reduced hierarchy counts. These are substantive mathematical definitions, although neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 emphasizes domain-invariant textual queries, domain-shift generalization and the dual-query decoder. V3 centers dataset/image-conditioned domain awareness and decoder-layer consistency, adding a claim of first consistency-driven refinement within a mask-transformer framework. The broad claim of strong low-label performance across four benchmarks remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations involving dataset-specific semantics, accumulated decoder misalignment, soft relevance weighting avoiding discarded true positives, and downweighting strong augmentations to preserve domain awareness. Its interpretations increasingly distinguish spatial gating from token-similarity attention. V2's explicit limitation about inherited CLIP biases and classes absent from training disappears, although a narrower Cityscapes small-object caveat remains.

D1.justification: V3 specifies frozen GPT-4o, four descriptions per dataset-class, objective weights, the 0.95 confidence threshold, segmentation-loss coefficients and temperature. Appendix A.1 supplies dataset attributes and their generation procedure; A.2-A.4 document refinement and loss implementation. V3 also promises future GitHub code/results without supplying a repository link. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although ambiguities remain.

R1.justification: Previously cited TQDM becomes the explicit baseline and source of inherited losses, with its one-way alignment and domain-generalization focus defining the proposed distinction. V3 adds substantive positioning against Pseudo-SD and references for POS and GPT-4o. The earlier broader query-design discussion is replaced by a more focused account of language-driven segmentation and domain awareness.

P1.justification: The title and framework name change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Method components receive numbered subsections, the narrative is reorganized around domain awareness and consistency, and a structured supplement is added. This exceeds terminology updates or edits accompanying new results alone.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. V2's wide benchmark table is split and reoriented into v3 Tables 2-3; Figure 2 is redrawn, and the separate regularization diagrams disappear. Existing qualitative examples are retained and relocated, including Figure 5 becoming Figure 3, while new analysis tables and five supplementary qualitative figures substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: V3 improves scrutiny through targeted ablations, clearer TQDM attribution and fuller implementation documentation. However, identical Figure 1 predictions change attribution from SemiVL to UniMatch V2 without explanation, ADE20K gains conflict with Table 3, and the new class-consistency mixture is ambiguous in A.3.2. The explicit CLIP-bias limitation also disappears. The PDFs cannot resolve whether key comparative evidence was corrected or misattributed, so the documentation gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
